title: Rust sqlx order repository
context: Order repository on sqlx and PostgreSQL. `search` filters by a status string that comes straight from the customer. `place_order` must decrement stock and insert the order atomically and must never oversell, even when many orders for the same SKU run concurrently; qty is validated as positive by the caller. Database errors must be returned to the caller.
code: pub async fn search(pool: &PgPool, status: &str, limit: i64) -> sqlx::Result<Vec<Order>> {
let sql = format!("SELECT id, sku, qty, status FROM orders WHERE status = '{status}' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT $1");
.map(|r| Order { id: r.get("id"), sku: r.get("sku"), qty: r.get("qty"), status: r.get("status") })
pub async fn place_order(pool: &PgPool, sku: &str, qty: i32) -> sqlx::Result<i64> {
let stock: i32 = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT stock FROM products WHERE sku = $1")
sqlx::query("UPDATE products SET stock = stock - $1 WHERE sku = $2")
let id: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar("INSERT INTO orders (sku, qty, status) VALUES ($1, $2, 'pending') RETURNING id")
pub async fn cancel(pool: &PgPool, id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<()> {
let _ = sqlx::query("UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id = $1").bind(id).execute(pool).await;

expected.why: customer-supplied status is interpolated into the SQL text (injection); it must be bound as a parameter
the row is read without FOR UPDATE, so concurrent orders all see the same stock, pass the check and oversell
the insert runs on the pool, outside the transaction, so it is not atomic with the stock update
tx is never committed; it is rolled back on drop, so the stock decrement is lost while the order stays inserted
the query result is discarded, so a database error is swallowed and cancel reports success
